sources.name: Ames Stereo Pipeline (ASP)
sources.description: Open-source stereo photogrammetry suite that builds DEMs and orthoimages from planetary orbital stereo pairs (LRO NAC, HiRISE, CTX, Kaguya and others). Works with ISIS camera models.

sources.name: Ceres Dawn FC HAMO global color shaded mosaic (60 ppd)
sources.description: DLR-produced Dawn Framing Camera HAMO color-shaded global map of Ceres at 60 pixels per degree.
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Mars Viking MDIM 2.1 color mosaic (232 m)
sources.description: Global color mosaic of Mars from Viking Orbiter images, with MOLA control. Classic base map for Mars.
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Mars MGS MOLA DEM mosaic (463 m)
sources.description: Global Mars elevation model from MOLA, resampled to 463 m/px in a simple cylindrical projection as GeoTIFF.
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Mars THEMIS daytime IR mosaic v12 (100 m)
sources.description: ASU global THEMIS daytime infrared mosaic of Mars, widely used as a basemap for geologic mapping.
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Mercury MESSENGER MDIS basemap (166 m)
sources.description: Global monochrome basemap reduced data record mosaic of Mercury from MESSENGER's MDIS.
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Moon Kaguya LALT shaded relief (512 ppd)
sources.description: Global lunar shaded relief from Kaguya laser altimeter data at 512 pixels per degree.
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Moon LRO LOLA global DEM (118 m)
sources.description: Global lunar elevation model from LOLA at 256 pixels per degree (about 118 m/px).
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Moon LRO LROC WAC global mosaic (100 m)
sources.description: Global 100 m/px normalized reflectance mosaic of the Moon from the LRO Wide Angle Camera (June 2013 release).
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Titan Cassini ISS global mosaic (4 km)
sources.description: Global near-infrared Cassini ISS mosaic of Titan's surface at 4 km/px, a standard Titan basemap.
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Venus Magellan C3-MDIR global mosaic (4641 m)
sources.description: Global Magellan radar image mosaic of Venus at 4641 m/px.
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Vesta Dawn FC HAMO global mosaic (74 ppd)
sources.description: Dawn Framing Camera HAMO global mosaic of Vesta at 74 pixels per degree.
sources.notes: Astropedia is a single-page app that returns HTTP 200 for any path, so the record URL could not be machine-verified.

sources.name: Mars Orbital Data / Image Explorer (THEMIS, CTX...)
sources.provider: Arizona State University Mars Space Flight Facility
sources.description: ASU web search interface for THEMIS (and other) Mars image products with filters for location, local time, resolution, solar longitude and processing stage. Download links per product.

sources.name: Europa Galileo stereo DTMs (AWS)
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (on AWS Open Data)
sources.description: Stereo-derived digital terrain models of five Europa sites (Agenor Linea, Cilix, Pwyll, Rhadamanthys Linea, Yelland Linea) tied to the controlled Galileo image set.

sources.name: Europa Galileo and Voyager controlled observations (AWS)
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (on AWS Open Data)
sources.description: Globally controlled Galileo SSI and Voyager images of Europa as COGs with improved pointing, ready for GIS use.

sources.name: Europa Galileo sequence mosaics (AWS)
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (on AWS Open Data)
sources.description: Controlled mosaics of Galileo SSI sequences of Europa as COGs.

sources.name: Kaguya Terrain Camera observations (COG on AWS)
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (on AWS Open Data)
sources.description: JAXA SELENE/Kaguya Terrain Camera stereo and mono images processed by USGS into COGs with STAC metadata. Global lunar coverage at about 10 m/px.

sources.name: Kaguya TC USGS DTMs (COG on AWS)
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (on AWS Open Data)
sources.description: Stereo digital terrain models and orthoimages from Kaguya Terrain Camera data produced with the Ames Stereo Pipeline, in equatorial and both polar projections.

sources.name: LOLA shot-level data (COG/Parquet on AWS)
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (on AWS Open Data)
sources.description: Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter individual laser shot data in cloud-friendly form with STAC index. For custom DEM building and profile extraction.

sources.name: THEMIS IR controlled mosaics (COG on AWS)
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (on AWS Open Data)
sources.description: Controlled THEMIS infrared (daytime and night) mosaics of Mars as COGs. Regional and global tiles tied to MOLA control.

sources.name: GDAL PDS3 raster driver
sources.description: GDAL driver that reads PDS3 image files as georeferenced rasters; sibling drivers read PDS4, ISIS2, ISIS3 and VICAR. Lets QGIS and GDAL tools open many planetary images.

sources.name: Apollo Surface Panoramas
sources.description: Stitched panoramas from Apollo 11-17 surface Hasselblad photographs, with large image downloads.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: Arecibo Radar Observations of Asteroids (LPI)
sources.description: LPI page listing Arecibo planetary radar observations and results for near-Earth asteroids, with images and links. Reference to radar imagery of small bodies.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: Consolidated Lunar Atlas
sources.description: Digitized Consolidated Lunar Atlas of Earth-based photographs by the Lunar and Planetary Laboratory, with images from Lick, Mt. Wilson and other observatories.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: Lunar Surface Flyovers
sources.description: Video flyovers of lunar landing sites and features built from LRO and Apollo-era data.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: LPI Lunar Images and Maps hub
sources.description: Index to LPI's lunar image atlases and maps: Lunar Orbiter, Apollo, Ranger, Consolidated Lunar Atlas, lunar map catalog, south pole atlas, rilles atlas and surface flyovers.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: Lunar Map Catalog
sources.description: Catalog of lunar maps (geologic, topographic and photomosaic) published by USGS, NASA and others, with links to scans.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: Lunar Orbiter Photo Gallery
sources.description: Scanned Lunar Orbiter I-V photographs (1966-1967) with index maps and per-frame viewers. Film scans, not the recovered tape data.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: Lunar Sample Atlas (Apollo sample photographs)
sources.description: Photographs and descriptions of Apollo and Luna returned lunar samples, including thin-section images. Sample images rather than orbital remote sensing.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: Lunar South Pole Atlas
sources.description: LPI atlas of south polar region maps and imagery (LOLA topography, LROC, illumination) for landing site studies.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: Ranger Photographs of the Moon
sources.description: Digitized Ranger 7, 8 and 9 lunar impact approach photographs, including the final frames before impact.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: South Pole-Aitken Basin Landing Site Database
sources.description: Interactive database of candidate landing sites in the South Pole-Aitken Basin with linked maps and imagery.
sources.notes: Server blocks non-browser scripts with HTTP 403; verified with a browser-style request via curl.

sources.name: NASA Eyes on the Solar System
sources.description: Browser-based 3D solar system viewer with spacecraft models, trajectories and body textures. Visualization and orientation only, not raw data.

sources.name: NASA Open APIs (api.nasa.gov)
sources.description: Free keyed REST APIs for NASA data including APOD, Mars Rover Photos, EPIC Earth images and the Image and Video Library. A free API key from the site is required (DEMO_KEY is rate-limited).

sources.name: PDS Data Release Announcements
sources.description: Chronological list of new and updated PDS data releases across all nodes, announced via the PDS subscription service. Use it to spot recent deliveries (2024-2026 missions and reprocessed products).

sources.name: PDS Data Search (beta 2.0, incl. ESA PSA holdings)
sources.description: New cross-node PDS data search that also includes mission data from ESA's Planetary Science Archive alongside PDS holdings. Search PDS4 bundles and collections by target, mission and instrument. Backed by the PDS Registry search API.

sources.name: PDS DOI Search
sources.description: Search service for Digital Object Identifiers assigned to PDS data products and bundles. Resolves a citation DOI to the archived data set.

sources.name: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS)
sources.description: Home of the NASA PDS, the official archive of NASA planetary mission data, run by seven discipline nodes. Links to data search, the tool registry, data standards (PDS3/PDS4) and every node. Entry point to everything below.

sources.name: PDS Data Set / Bundle Keyword Search
sources.description: Keyword search for PDS3 data sets and PDS4 bundles and collections across all nodes. Returns links to the owning node's landing page and download location. Good for finding a data set by mission, instrument or target name.

sources.name: Peppi - PDS Search API Python client
sources.description: Python library giving pythonic query syntax for exploring PDS4 data through the PDS Search API. Useful for scripting discovery of imagery products by target and mission.

sources.name: PDS Registry Search API (PDS4)
sources.description: REST search API over the PDS4 registry: query products, collections and bundles by target, mission, instrument and time. Documentation lives on GitHub Pages; the live endpoint is /api/search/1/ on pds.mcp.nasa.gov. Returns JSON labels with direct file URLs.

sources.name: PDS Tool Registry
sources.description: Registry of software for searching, accessing and using PDS3 and PDS4 data, including community-contributed packages. Starting point for readers, viewers and converters.

sources.name: PDS Transform Tool
sources.description: Command-line tool that converts PDS3 and PDS4 product labels and data into common formats such as PNG, FITS and CSV. Handy when a viewer cannot open a PDS image directly.

sources.name: Bennu Trek
sources.description: Bennu Trek serves OSIRIS-REx image mosaics, shape model and DEM layers. Free, no login; tiles are also reachable through WMTS.

sources.name: Icy Moons Trek
sources.description: Icy Moons Trek covers the Galilean moons with Voyager and Galileo mosaics and maps. Free, no login; tiles are also reachable through WMTS.

sources.name: MoonDiff - lunar change detection portal
sources.description: Citizen-science portal for comparing old and new orbital lunar images to find new craters and missing spacecraft hardware. Requires sign-up to participate, but browsing examples is open.

sources.name: Phobos Trek
sources.description: Phobos Trek serves Mars Express and MRO-derived mosaics and shape-model layers. Free, no login; tiles are also reachable through WMTS.

sources.name: NASA Solar System Treks (Trek portal)
sources.description: Family of browser-based 2D and 3D web portals for planetary mapping, each with layered global basemaps, DEMs, measurement and slope tools, exports and a WMTS tile service. Covers the bodies listed on the portal; each is a separate entry below.

sources.name: Ryugu Trek
sources.description: Ryugu Trek serves Hayabusa2 image mosaics and shape-model derived layers. Free, no login; tiles are also reachable through WMTS.

sources.name: NSSDCA Master Catalog
sources.provider: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (GSFC)
sources.description: NASA's catalog of spacecraft, experiments and data sets from 1957 onward, with links to archived data. Key for pre-PDS and heritage missions (Mariner, Lunar Orbiter, Ranger, Apollo, Pioneer) and for finding archive locations.

sources.name: NSSDCA Photo Gallery
sources.provider: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (GSFC)
sources.description: Curated collection of spacecraft and planetary images, including Apollo, Voyager, Mariner, Pioneer and Viking, organised by target and mission. Browse-quality images, not science archives.

sources.name: NSSDCA Planetary Science pages
sources.provider: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (GSFC)
sources.description: NSSDCA planetary hub with fact sheets, mission summaries and links to archived image and data collections for solar system bodies.

sources.name: OpenPlanetary community
sources.description: Community hub for open-source planetary science software, data and events, including tools for reading and mapping planetary data.

sources.name: pdr - Planetary Data Reader (Python)
sources.description: Python library that opens PDS3 and PDS4 data products (images, tables, cubes) as numpy arrays and pandas objects from a label, with support for many mission-specific formats. Install from PyPI as pdr.

sources.name: PDS Planetary Image Atlas
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Search interface for image products across the Imaging Node holdings by target, mission, instrument, time and footprint. Results link to downloadable PDS files and labels. Supersedes the older Image Atlas at pds-imaging.jpl.nasa.gov/search/.

sources.name: PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (IMG)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: The PDS discipline node for planetary images and cartographic products, hosted by JPL with USGS Astrogeology. Holds data from Mariner, Viking, Voyager, Galileo, Cassini, Magellan, Clementine, MGS, MRO, MER, MSL, Mars 2020, Juno and more.

sources.name: Cassini cartographic maps (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Cartographic map products and global mosaics of Saturnian moons derived from Cassini ISS. Map-projected image files with PDS labels.

sources.name: Galileo SSI and NIMS (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Galileo Solid State Imager REDRs and NIMS EDRs and cubes of the Jovian system, Gaspra, Ida, the Moon and Venus.

sources.name: Juno JunoCam and SRU (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: JunoCam EDR and RDR images of Jupiter and its moons, plus stellar reference unit data. Includes Ganymede, Europa and Io flyby images.

sources.name: Mariner 6 and 7 (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Reduced data records of the Mariner 6 and 7 Mars flyby television images.

sources.name: Mariner 9 (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Mariner 9 television EDRs, the first images from Mars orbit and of Phobos and Deimos.

sources.name: Mars Express HRSC (PDS Imaging copy)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: PDS-hosted copy of ESA Mars Express HRSC RDRs, map-projected images and orthophoto/DTM products. ESA PSA remains the primary source.

sources.name: Mars Odyssey THEMIS (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: THEMIS visible and infrared EDRs and RDRs of Mars. The IR day and night mosaics are built from these.

sources.name: Voyager ISS (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Voyager 1 and 2 imaging EDRs for Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune systems, plus calibrated Saturn products. The only close-up imagery of Uranus, Neptune and Triton.

sources.name: NAIF - SPICE Navigation and Ancillary Information
sources.provider: NASA PDS Navigation and Ancillary Information Facility (JPL)
sources.description: Home of SPICE kernels (spacecraft and planet ephemerides, pointing, instrument geometry) needed to geometrically process raw planetary images in ISIS. Supporting data only; contains no imagery itself.

sources.name: Orbital Data Explorer - Mercury
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Washington University in St. Louis)
sources.description: PDS Geosciences Orbital Data Explorer (ODE) for Mercury: footprint-based search and map interface over orbital instrument products (imagery, spectrometer cubes, altimetry, radar) with direct PDS download links. Has a documented REST API (oderest.rsl.wustl.edu).

sources.name: ODE REST web service (oderest)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Washington University in St. Louis)
sources.description: Programmatic REST interface to ODE product and footprint queries for Mars, the Moon, Mercury and Venus. Returns XML or JSON listings with download URLs. Used by the OpenReSense ODE connector.

sources.name: Orbital Data Explorer - Venus
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Washington University in St. Louis)
sources.description: PDS Geosciences Orbital Data Explorer (ODE) for Venus: footprint-based search and map interface over orbital instrument products (imagery, spectrometer cubes, altimetry, radar) with direct PDS download links. Has a documented REST API (oderest.rsl.wustl.edu).

sources.name: PDS Planetary Plasma Interactions Node (PPI)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Planetary Plasma Interactions Node (UCLA)
sources.description: PDS node for particles-and-fields data (magnetometer, plasma, radio). Mostly not imagery, but it holds Juno, Cassini and Voyager aurora and radio data useful alongside images; included as a supporting archive.

sources.name: Voyager (RMS)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Voyager imaging and photopolarimeter/UVS ring occultation volumes with geometry indexes.

sources.name: SBN archive bulk directories (PDS3 and PDS4)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: Direct HTTPS directory listings for SBN PDS4 bundles, with a sibling PDS3 tree. Use for bulk downloads of small-body image collections.

sources.name: Dawn Framing Camera - Ceres raw and calibrated images
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: Dawn Framing Camera Level 1 raw and calibrated images of Ceres in PDS4 format, from approach through LAMO orbit.

sources.name: Dawn Framing Camera - Vesta raw and calibrated images
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: Dawn Framing Camera Level 1 raw and calibrated images of Vesta from approach through HAMO and LAMO orbits.

sources.name: Dawn global image mosaics of Ceres
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: Dawn Framing Camera global image mosaics of Ceres, map-projected with PDS4 labels.

sources.name: Dawn global image mosaics of Vesta
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: Dawn Framing Camera global image mosaics of Vesta, map-projected with PDS4 labels.

sources.name: Europa Clipper data (SBN)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: SBN landing page for data from the Europa Clipper mission, launched October 2024, including cruise and flyby calibration observations. Science-phase Europa data are expected from 2030.

sources.name: SBN image data sets (browse by data type)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: SBN list of every archived image data set (spacecraft and ground-based) of small bodies. Useful to find individual imagery sets such as NEAR MSI, Dawn FC and Hayabusa AMICA.

sources.name: SBN map and mosaic data sets
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: SBN list of map and mosaic products: Dawn global mosaics and spectral maps of Vesta and Ceres, NEAR Eros image maps and Stooke small-body maps.

sources.name: NEAR Shoemaker MSI (Eros) at SBN
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: NEAR Multispectral Imager images of 433 Eros and 253 Mathilde, plus Eros image maps. Eros images with geometry backplanes are also provided.

sources.name: PDS Small Bodies Node - PSI (asteroid/dust subnode)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: Planetary Science Institute site of the PDS Small Bodies Node with browse-by-mission, data-type and target-type views of the SBN archive. Contains per-dataset pages for Dawn, OSIRIS-REx, Hayabusa2, NEAR, Galileo asteroid flybys and ground-based surveys.

sources.name: Small Bodies Image Browser (SBIB)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: Browser for image products in the SBN archive, searchable by target and mission, with thumbnails and links to the underlying PDS files.

sources.name: Stooke small-body maps and shape models
sources.provider: NASA PDS Small Bodies Node (University of Maryland / Planetary Science Institute)
sources.description: Philip Stooke's maps and shape models of irregular satellites, asteroids and comet nuclei, derived from spacecraft images and archived at SBN.

sources.name: PDS Geosciences Spectral Library
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Washington University in St. Louis)
sources.description: Laboratory reflectance and emission spectra of minerals, meteorites and analogs from RELAB, USGS and ASU, used to interpret CRISM, OMEGA, M3 and TES data. Point spectra, not imagery, but essential for mineral mapping.

sources.name: PDS4 Viewer and pds4-tools
sources.description: Standalone desktop viewer for PDS4 images, tables and headers (Windows, macOS, Linux) and the pds4-tools Python package behind it. Best for quick inspection of PDS4 products.

sources.name: planetarypy (Python)
sources.description: Community effort to develop a core Python package ecosystem for planetary science, with a list of affiliated packages for working with planetary data. Documentation content is CC BY-SA 4.0. Complements the separately catalogued pdr reader.
sources.notes: Which packages read which formats was not verified.

sources.name: Planetary Science Institute (PSI)
sources.description: Home of PSI, which runs the Small Bodies Node asteroid/dust subnode and the SBIB image browser. Use the SBN entries for data; this page is the institutional entry.

sources.name: QGIS planetary plugins (ISIS3 tag)
sources.description: QGIS plugin repository listing for ISIS3 and planetary tools such as the USGS Astrogeology POW plugin, helping load planetary cubes and web services in QGIS.

sources.name: ALE - Abstraction Library for Ephemerides
sources.description: USGS library that builds camera models from PDS labels and SPICE kernels, used by ISIS and CSM to georeference raw planetary images.

sources.name: USGS Astrogeology STAC API
sources.description: STAC 1.1 API over analysis-ready planetary data in the cloud: Galileo and Voyager controlled observations, HiRISE, CTX and Kaguya TC DTMs, THEMIS mosaics and LOLA shots. Items link to Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs and cumulative index parquet files on AWS.

sources.name: USGS Astrogeology STAC Browser
sources.description: Web browser for the USGS Astrogeology STAC catalog with map previews and asset links for planetary COG and DEM collections.

sources.name: USGS Astrogeology Science Center
sources.description: Home of USGS planetary cartography, geologic mapping, ISIS software and the Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node of the PDS. Entry page for Astropedia, PILOT, Map-a-Planet, POW, STAC and web map services.

sources.name: Astrolink - USGS Astrogeology archive facility
sources.description: USGS Astrogeology's archival facility for planetary mission data and products. The linked AstroCloud site is the USGS online front end for Astro tools such as Map-A-Planet 2 and POW.

sources.name: Astropedia - Lunar and Planetary Cartographic Catalog
sources.description: Searchable catalog of USGS and community-contributed planetary maps, global mosaics, DEMs, geologic maps and GIS layers for the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, asteroids and outer-planet moons. Each record has download links (GeoTIFF, ISIS cube, shapefile) and metadata.

sources.name: AutoCNet - planetary image control networks
sources.description: USGS Python tool for tie-point matching and bundle adjustment of planetary images, used to produce controlled mosaics.

sources.name: ISIS - Integrated Software for Imagers and Spectrometers
sources.description: USGS software to ingest, radiometrically calibrate, geometrically process and map-project raw planetary images from dozens of missions into ISIS3 cubes and GeoTIFFs. Needs SPICE kernels and the ISIS data area; Linux/macOS or WSL.

sources.name: Map-A-Planet 2 (MAP2)
sources.description: Web service that cuts, reprojects and downloads user-chosen subsets of USGS global mosaics and DEMs as GeoTIFF/ISIS cubes in a selectable map projection. Fast way to get a georeferenced clip of a mosaic without desktop software.

sources.name: USGS Astrogeology PDS archive (pdsimage2.wr.usgs.gov)
sources.description: USGS-hosted PDS mission data volumes (Cartography node mirror) with per-mission directories for Mars, Moon and outer-planet cartographic products.

sources.name: PILOT - Planetary Image Locator Tool
sources.description: Footprint-based image search across the PDS Imaging holdings for the Moon, Mars, Mercury and outer-planet moons, with filters for resolution, phase, time and geometry. Produces download lists and feeds POW for projection.

sources.name: USGS Planetary Analysis Ready Data (ARD) documentation
sources.description: Documentation pages per planetary cloud dataset (Mars HiRISE, CTX DTMs, THEMIS mosaics; Moon Kaguya TC, LOLA; Europa Galileo and Voyager), with tutorials and code examples for reading COGs.

sources.name: USGS Planetary Geologic Mapping Program

links.label: Unified Geologic Map of the Moon (SIM 3316)

sources.description: Program page cataloguing NASA-funded planetary geologic maps (USGS SIM series) with PDFs and GIS data. Maps of the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Vesta and Jovian moons are available as GIS downloads.

sources.name: POW - Projection on the Web
sources.description: Cloud service that calibrates, geometrically processes and map-projects raw PDS images chosen in PILOT using ISIS, delivering GeoTIFF/ISIS cubes by email link. No local ISIS install needed, with selectable output resolution, bands and projection.
